items.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019
items.q: My favorite trumpet player is Louis Armstrong. Not because — well a couple of reasons. Louis Armstrong — there’s never been another trumpet player to really duplicate that sound that he has.

ctx.x: Well it turned out to be a pretty high key also.

Yes it did, yes it did. So that was a lot of fun. That was a lot of fun. But yeah it’s pretty physical. Everything — it’s one of the reasons why I love playing the trumpet. It goes — it kind of goes through my whole body you know. I feel it. When I play it goes through everything. It goes through the physical aspect, it goes through my brain, it goes through © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

my soul, it goes through everything, and what comes out, every time I play, is something unique and different. And I embrace that too. I don’t want to really — how do I put this the right way? I don’t want to duplicate anything that I’ve done before because I’ve done that already. You know what I mean? So when I’m playing, every note, every solo, every phrase has its own — a life of its own. And I kind of dig that. You know what I mean? My favorite trumpet player is Louis Armstrong.
